text:
alex: CI red on main after a poetry lock regen — integration suite failing on ubuntu-latest. quick: ImportError: cannot import name 'files' from 'importlib_resources' so a bunch of runtime imports blow up. link to run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/12345678

ci-bot: GH Actions run failed — tests/integration/test_storage.py::TestBlobLifecycle::test_upload (see logs). job 'linux-integration' exited 1. cache: restored pip wheels from cache key 'poetry-wheels-2026-03-17'.

sam: can you paste the traceback snippet? local repro?

alex: repro locally in a py310 venv using the lockfile. snippet:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../site-packages/storage/client.py", line 23, in <module>
    from importlib_resources import files
ImportError: cannot import name 'files' from 'importlib_resources' (/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/importlib_resources/__init__.py)
```

maria: that API (files) moved to importlib_resources 6.x I think — older 5.x had different names. did the lock regen pick a newer transitive?

alex: lockfile was regenerated earlier today as part of a deps sweep (no manual package changes). poetry.lock shows importlib-resources 5.10.0 -> now 6.1.2 as transitive via some package.

sam: can we bisect to find the transitive chain quickly? if it's only a transitive pin we can patch constraints. @dev-infra any chance the runner cached wheels are causing a mismatch? cache key suggests older wheels restored before new lock.

dev-infra: looking. cache key used: poetry-wheels-2026-03-17. If the lock changed after cache was populated GH will still restore older wheel artifacts. I can purge the runner cache for that workflow and re-run — will do if you want.

leo: quick workaround: add a constraints override in pyproject to force importlib-resources==6.1.2 (or the min supported) and bump lock, that'll silence for now while we bisect. but prefer to find the root cause.

alex: failing tests: tests/integration/test_storage.py::TestBlobLifecycle::test_upload and tests/unit/test_config_loader.py::test_load_from_pkg_resources. both hit import paths.

sam: if you'll allow, I'll run a lockfile bisect across the repo history to find when the transitive changed. should take ~20m. alex can you ping me if you want me to start now?

alex: please start now, thanks. I left my machine building slow.

sam: running quick script now:
```
# bisect sketch (local)
git checkout main~50..main
for rev in $(git rev-list --max-count=50 main); do
  git checkout $rev -- poetry.lock
  poetry install -n --no-root --no-interaction
  poetry run pytest tests/integration/test_storage.py::TestBlobLifecycle::test_upload -q || { echo "bad:$rev"; break; }
done
```
first bad rev: 1f3a9e2 -> introduced bump in 'fastapi-utils' dependency which pulls importlib-resources ^6.

maria: aha. fastapi-utils bumped a dependency. probably safe to pin importlib-resources for the short term but we should update code to use stdlib importlib.resources.files where possible (py310+), or ensure compat shim.

dev-infra: cache purge done. kicked a rerun of the failing job. new run id: 12345679.

ci-bot: rerun started, restoring caches: poetry-wheels-2026-03-18 (fresh).

alex: rerun still red — same import error. so it's not a stale wheel cache causing the mismatch; lock truly moved the transitive.

sam: I opened a small PR that pins importlib-resources==6.1.2 in pyproject.toml (constraints section) + lock regen. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pull/7890 — can someone review quickly?

leo: reviewing now. small nit about the comment, otherwise LGTM. this will buy time. add a note in the changelog and a TODO to remove the pin when we migrate to stdlib importlib.resources.

maria: also adding a unit test that explicitly imports files from both importlib.resources and importlib_resources to detect regressions in CI.

alex: thanks. if sam's bisect says fastapi-utils update is the cause, we should coordinate with the team that bumped it — maybe they intended the bump. I'll follow up in that PR with the bisect details. :thumbsup:

sam: bisect confirmed: commit 1f3a9e2 (deps: bump fastapi-utils 0.9.1 -> 0.10.0) brought importlib-resources ^6. So it's an upstream transitive decision. I'll add the bisect result to the PR description and mark as temporary pin.

dev-infra: once PR merges I'll trigger a full integration rerun without caches to confirm green.

ci-bot: workflow run queued by PR merge.

alex: resolved for now via pin + tests. follow-up: roadmap item to migrate code paths to stdlib importlib.resources or add compatibility layer. created ticket INFRA-213.

sam: great triage, nice teamwork.

maria: :thumbsup:

leo: closing loop — leaving a short note in #release-notes about the temporary pin and promise to remove later.

alex: thanks all — I'll watch the merged run and unassign myself once green.
